title: Enhancing the Energy Performance of Integrated Photovoltaic and Air-Source Heat Pump Systems Using Smart Control and Thermal Energy Storage
content: This study investigates the energy performance of photovoltaic system cooperating with an air-source heat pump (PV-ASHP) systems integrated with thermal energy storage (TES) for residential heating and cooling under two different Greek climatic conditions. Annual simulations were carried out using TRNSYS for reference dwelling in Athens and Kastoria. A parametric analysis examined the influence of TES capacity, storage temperature setpoints and PV power thresholds on system performance. The results were compared with those of a corresponding system without TES integration. The results demonstrate that TES integration can improve the annual performance of PV-ASHP systems. The annual seasonal performance factor increased from 3.56 to 4.71 in Athens and from 3.01 to 4.02 in Kastoria. The corresponding annual solar fractions reached 54% and 46%, respectively. The findings also highlight the influence of climatic conditions and system operating parameters on the optimal configuration and overall energy performance. This study provides a comparative assessment of PV-ASHP systems incorporating thermal storage for both heating and cooling applications in two distinct climatic regions. It demonstrates the potential of TES and PV-based energy management to improve system performance and reduce dependence on grid electricity.
